samples.summary: Rewritten store-level `undo()`/`redo()` still carry no `assertWritable()` guard, unlike every other `doc.update()` path in the same file
samples.evidence: `replayHistory()` (yorkie-store.ts:1305) calls `this.doc.history.undo()`, which is a CRDT write on the attached document and goes out on the next PushPull with verb `rw`. Every other write this store exposes is gated: `updateSelection` (:661), `ensureAxisOrder` (:699) and all five comment mutators via `assertWritable` (:1380-1384). That guard's own doc-comment states the design rule — "a UI gate is the wrong last line: this throws so a future caller that forgets it fails loudly instead of writing where the Yorkie auth webhook will refuse it and wedge the viewer's sync." The undo path is the exception: the only gates are `Spreadsheet.undo/redo` (`spreadsheet.ts:650,664`) and the two keyboard handlers (`worksheet.ts:5106,5120`). I could not find a currently-reachable UI path that calls `store.undo()` on a read-only mount, so this is defence-in-depth rather than a live bypass — but this change adds two NEW public entry points around the same subsystem (`Spreadsheet.onUndoTabJump`, `Spreadsheet.focusUndoSelection`, spreadsheet.ts:678,689) neither of which checks `_readOnly`, so the un-guarded surface grew while the store-level guard was not added. Attack shape if a future caller (or the harness/bridge) reaches it on a share-link `viewer` mount: the viewer emits an `rw` change the Yorkie auth webhook refuses, wedging their sync, and in the deployment posture where `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is false (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:176-183, shadow mode) the write is actually accepted.
searchedFor: grep `\.undo\(|\.redo\(` across packages (excluding tests) to enumerate every caller of Store.undo/Sheet.undo/Spreadsheet.undo

samples.summary: `selection.tabId`, parsed out of a CRDT operation path by splitting on `.`, is fed straight to `setActiveTabId` and then used as an object index with no membership check
samples.evidence: `handleUndoJump` does `setActiveTabId(selection.tabId)` without checking the id against `root.tabOrder`/`root.tabs`. The id originates in `parseSheetPath` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/undo-selection.ts:74-87), which just slices `$.sheets.` off the path and splits on the first `.` — the comment asserts tab ids never contain `.`, which holds for `generateTabId()` output but is not validated anywhere on ingest (e.g. imported/migrated documents, or a collaborator writing an arbitrary key under `root.sheets`). Downstream the value is used as a raw object key: `root.tabs[activeTabId]` (document-detail.tsx:669) and `new YorkieStore(doc, tabId)` → `root.sheets[this.tabId]` (yorkie-store.ts:1406). A key such as `__proto__`/`constructor` therefore resolves to a prototype object rather than a worksheet, and a misparsed/deleted tab id switches the editor to a tab that does not exist. I could not complete an exploit chain — the op paths consumed here come only from the local client's own undo replay, so an attacker cannot inject them directly — hence low confidence. Cheap fix: only switch when `root.tabs` has an own property for the id (`Object.hasOwn`).
searchedFor: grep `setActiveTabId` and `activeTabId` in document-detail.tsx to find every sink
grep `new YorkieStore\(` to see how tabId reaches root.sheets indexing

samples.summary: New lessons doc publishes a step-by-step recipe for forging an authenticated session cookie (sign a JWT with `JWT_SECRET`, set `wafflebase_session`, `tokenType: 'access'`)
samples.evidence: Lines 85-90 document how to mint a signed session for an arbitrary user: "sign a JWT with the backend's `JWT_SECRET` and set it as the `wafflebase_session` cookie... The payload needs **`tokenType: 'access'`** — `JwtStrategy.validate` refuses anything else". No secret value is leaked (JWT_SECRET stays in env, and `packages/backend/src/template/seed/register-templates.ts` already does this under guards that refuse non-local origins, :94). The exposure is therefore informational only: it normalises OAuth-bypass-by-cookie-minting as a routine dev workflow and hands an attacker who has obtained JWT_SECRET (staging/shared secret reuse) the exact impersonation payload shape. Worth a pointer to the guarded seed script instead of an inline recipe.
searchedFor: grep JWT_SECRET/wafflebase_session/tokenType in the new lessons doc
grep JWT_SECRET across packages/backend/src for hardcoded or defaulted secrets
